title: review: constraints.grant_scope: a fix round may carry extra scope entries that the scope guard, the packet and the daemon dirty-scope check honour, so the Planner widens scope without a respec
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label E7 (analysis 2026-10-01). Today a fix round inherits the held task's scope (daemon.auto_fix_round passes current['scope']); when the fix needs one more file (A1 and A6 in wave 1 died on pinned tests outside scope) the Planner must supersede and refile the whole task.

Facts (goal/T-1403 at 92c1a98 plus B5 merged before this task; B8 is parked, so spawn.py is as on goal/T-1403; re-check line numbers by symbol):
- .claude/hooks/scope-guard.sh:7-20 reads `.scope[]` of the task json and blocks Edit/Write outside it (exit 2).
- scopes.py:14-30 safe_scope(task, worktree) returns task.write_scope or task.scope entries contained in the worktree; spawn.py:812 renders write_scope into the packet from `scope`; daemon.py:1230-1249 _dirty_scope_paths(worktree, scope) and the gate's dirty check use task['scope']; several read-only modules (context_router.py:118, evidence.py:51, jev_skills.py:52, memory_hot.py:72, memory_scorecard.py:52, jev_sched.py:87) read scope or write_scope for ranking only and stay as they are.
- bus.create_task validates scope non-empty (TaskCreated hook); constraints is a free dict.

Change:
1. scopes.effective_scope(task) -> list: task['scope'] + (task.get('constraints') or {}).get('grant_scope') or [], deduplicated, order kept; grant entries go through the same containment rules as safe_scope. safe_scope uses effective_scope.
2. scope-guard.sh: also accept globs from `.constraints.grant_scope[]?` (same loop, both lists), and name both lists in the block message.
3. spawn packet (812): write_scope lists effective_scope; daemon gate dirty check and any other write-time scope read in daemon.py (grep "\\[\"scope\"\\]" and ".get(\"scope\")" in daemon.py and spawn.py) use scopes.effective_scope(task). auto_fix_round keeps copying scope and now also copies constraints.grant_scope (it already spreads constraints).
4. bus.create_task: when constraints.grant_scope is present, validate it is a list of non-empty relative path strings without '..' (ValueError otherwise) and record it in the creation event; no other bus change.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_scopes.py safe_scope tests (grep 'safe_scope') pass unchanged; the hook tests in tests/test_hooks.py or tests/test_scope_guard*.py (grep 'scope-guard' under tests/) pass unchanged and gain the grant case; tests/test_daemon.py dirty-scope gate tests (grep '_dirty_scope_paths' / 'executor did not commit'). Run tests/test_scopes.py, tests/test_spawn.py, tests/test_daemon.py, tests/test_bus.py and the hook tests.

Depends on B5 T-1554 (daemon.py chain). B8 T-1509 is parked (human 2026-10-03), so there is no spawn.py dependency. Out of scope: mcp.py, executor.py.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number. Every test named in the acceptance must exist in the diff; the gate checks for them by id.

Re-filed 2026-10-02 11:55 (replaces T-1513): B5 re-filed as T-1554; depends_on re-pointed to T-1554, T-1509; the first acceptance item describes the grant entry in words instead of quoting a test file path (E6v2's gate now demands any test path named in acceptance); spec and scope unchanged.

Re-filed 2026-10-03 (replaces T-1555): B8 parked by the human, depends_on drops T-1509; spec, acceptance and scope otherwise unchanged.
acceptance: tests/test_scopes.py::test_effective_scope_includes_grant_scope: passes: scopes.effective_scope of a task with scope ['a/'] and constraints.grant_scope naming one test module under tests/ returns both entries in order, safe_scope keeps the grant entry when it is contained in the worktree and drops '..' entries; a task without grant_scope is unchanged

tests/test_hooks.py::test_scope_guard_accepts_grant_scope: passes: scope-guard.sh allows a write to a path matched only by constraints.grant_scope and still blocks a path outside both lists with a message naming both

tests/test_daemon.py::test_gate_dirty_check_and_fix_round_honour_grant_scope: passes: a done execute task with an uncommitted file under its grant_scope is reported by the gate's dirty-scope check (held 'executor did not commit'), and auto_fix_round's fix round carries the parent's constraints.grant_scope

tests/test_bus.py::test_create_task_validates_grant_scope: passes: bus.create_task rejects grant_scope entries that are not strings, are empty, are absolute or contain '..', and accepts a list of relative paths

result.summary: The four named tests exist and match the acceptance wording. I did not run any tests. Two behaviour problems: safe_scope drops write_scope, and review diffs ignore granted paths.

comments.issue: safe_scope used to prefer task['write_scope'] over task['scope']. It now calls effective_scope, which never reads write_scope, so any task or packet carrying an explicit write_scope silently loses it. write_scope may be narrower than scope, or may exist without scope. This breaks the old behaviour, which the spec says must pass unchanged. Keep the write_scope-first branch and add grant_scope to it, or fall back to effective_scope only when write_scope is absent.

The review diff is built from src['scope'] only. Review tasks are created in daemon.py (around line 1359) with t['scope']. Files edited under constraints.grant_scope never appear in the reviewer's scoped diff. The security review of /orchestrator/*.py or hooks changes can therefore miss the granted files. Use effective_scope for the diff pathspec and for review task creation.

The _path_in_scope check for routine review comments uses held['scope'] only. A comment on a granted path is treated as out of scope, so such holds never get an automatic routine fix round. The spec asked for every write-time scope read in daemon.py to use effective_scope.

The hook test checks that the stderr message contains 'grant_scope', but it does not assert that the blocked path is rejected specifically because it matched neither list. It also does not cover the first block in scope-guard.sh, the early-exit path for files outside the worktree, which has a changed message. Coverage is thin but adequate.
